facts: Machine-wide Git for Windows layouts. A per-user install (no admin rights) lands under %LOCALAPPDATA% instead, and is found via git.exe below.
The WSL launcher ships at C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe whether or not a distro is installed, so it must never be mistaken for a usable bash.

Where bash lives on a Windows machine. Every surface that needs a shell, the SDK's run_terminal_command, the Desktop terminal panel, the Desktop's per-workspace startup script, asks this module, so they can never disagree about whether this machine has bash.

Looking in enough places is the whole job. An install that we fail to find is indistinguishable to the user from no install at all: they run the installer, we keep saying bash is missing, and the only conclusion available to them is that the app is broken.

The installer's per-user mode, which is what a user without admin rights gets, and what an agent installing Git on the user's behalf gets, since it is not elevated either. This one is why "it installed Git and still says bash is missing" was reachable at all.
entries.title: SDK update: WINDOWS
entries.summary: New files: `sdk/src/tools/windows-bash.ts`.

ai.title: SDK extracts Windows bash lookup into windows-bash.ts
ai.summary: The SDK's Windows bash resolution logic is moved from an inline function in sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts into a new sdk/src/tools/windows-bash.ts module, which run_terminal_command now imports and calls via findWindowsBash(processEnv). The finder derives candidate locations from environment variables (ProgramFiles, ProgramW6432, LOCALAPPDATA, USERPROFILE, SystemDrive/ProgramData, SCOOP, SCOOP_GLOBAL) instead of the previous hardcoded C:\ paths, and consults the registry only as a last resort after a filesystem search misses, so an install performed while the app is open is detected without a restart. This change was made because hardcoded C:\ literals made the lookup a function of the host rather than its env argument, which silently defeated fixture-based tests and reported bash as missing for per-user, Scoop, Chocolatey, and non-C: installs that the inline version missed.
ai.evidence: New file sdk/src/tools/windows-bash.ts defines findWindowsBash, windowsBashCandidates, pathExists, parseRegistryPath, resetGitRegistryCache, and createWindowsBashNotFoundError; run-terminal-command.ts now imports and calls findWindowsBash(processEnv) in place of its removed inline findWindowsBash, and creates the not-found error from the new module. The test file sdk/src/__tests__/windows-bash.test.ts asserts findWindowsBash against layouts including per-user installs under %LOCALAPPDATA%, Scoop, non-C: ProgramFiles, and PATH-local git.exe siblings. WINDOWS.md troubleshooting copy was updated to describe these same search locations.

eli5.text: Your automated tests used to give each step, including database setup, the same 5-second timeout, so when the test machine slowed down, the setup step itself would fail and blame a random test that had nothing to do with the failure. Now, setup steps that build real test databases get a separate, longer time limit, and when a test run flakes out (passes on retry), CI captures the name of the failing test instead of burying it in thousands of lines of log output, so you can quickly see which test actually stalled instead of guessing from a wall of text.

ai.title: SDK reports incomplete usage receipts and reasoning tokens
ai.summary: The SDK now exposes an `onUsageIncomplete` callback on `RunOptions`, called whenever a model request ends before an exact provider usage receipt arrives. `promptAiSdkStream` invokes `onUsageIncomplete` on stream abort, thrown response-body recovery, or when the finish part lacks usage data, instead of silently dropping the event; the agent runtime forwards it through `runAgentStep` as `onAgentUsageIncomplete`, and the agent-stream adapter passes it from `getAgentStreamFromTemplate`. `CacheDebugUsageData` also gains an optional `reasoningOutputTokens` field, populated from `outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens` in `emitCacheDebugUsage`. The change spans Shared/Core, Agent Runtime, and SDK across five files.
ai.evidence: Added `onUsageIncomplete` callback to `RunOptions` in `sdk/src/run.ts` and threaded it through `runAgentStep` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`; `promptAiSdkStream` in `sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` now invokes `onUsageIncomplete` when the stream ends without a final usage receipt (aborted signal, thrown recovery, or `finishInfo.hasUsage` false); new `reasoningOutputTokens` field added to `CacheDebugUsageData` in `common/src/types/contracts/llm.ts`, populated from `outputTokenDetails.reasoningTokens`; new test titles assert "reports an incomplete receipt when the stream ends without final usage", "reports an incomplete receipt when cancellation rejects the response body", and "does not turn a normal finish without usage into exact zeroes".
ai.migration: No action required; existing SDK consumers that do not set `onUsageIncomplete` continue to work unchanged.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that reads `onUsageIncomplete` to act on incomplete receipts (e.g. a billing or billing-proration host).

facts: This is the whole difference between this detector and the ones that were defeated: without `cf-ray` the header is caller-authored text on a request that never touched Cloudflare, which is exactly as forgeable as a self-reported fingerprint.

This one is stamped by OUR edge, on the request, describing the infrastructure that sent it. A caller cannot remove it, and adding it falsely only implicates themselves. That is what makes it safe enough to action automatically, and the reason every other signal here is still only a lead.
Raw `cf-ray` value. Absent means the request did not come through our Cloudflare edge, so the `cf-worker` value is not ours to trust.

ai.title: Add Cloudflare Worker egress detector for resold free capacity
ai.summary: A new module in `common/src/constants/cf-worker-signals.ts` defines a pure `detectCfWorker` function that keys on the `cf-worker` header stamped by the Cloudflare edge, requiring the companion `cf-ray` header to corroborate that the request traversed Freebuff's own edge before flagging a zone. The verdict type, `CfWorkerEvidence` record shape, `parseAllowedWorkerZones` allowlist parser, and `looksLikeProxyClientId` helper are defined and exported, along with the `CfWorkerMode` action ladder of `off`, `observe`, `block`, and `ban`, but no reader imports or enforces them in this commit. The detector exists to catch third-party Workers like `pingmike2/freebuff2api-wokers` that pool harvested tokens and resell free-mode capacity, while the zone allowlist is meant to spare Freebuff's own Workers such as `app-preview-proxy`.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/constants/cf-worker-signals.ts` adds the `detectCfWorker` function, the `CF_WORKER_HEADER` / `CF_RAY_HEADER` constants, and pure detection types with no wire-up to a request handler in this change.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which service or request handler calls `detectCfWorker`, how `CfWorkerMode` is read from operator configuration, or which consumer emits `CfWorkerEvidence` into the ban review dashboard.

ai.title: Clickable title box makes composer and queue titles clickable
ai.summary: Adds `ClickableTitleBox`, a memoized OpenTUI `<box>` wrapper that treats its top-border title as a button by tracking press state across `onMouseDown`/`onMouseUp` and invoking `onTitleClick` only for a button-0 click on the title row, then swaps it in as the outer element of the non-compact `ChatInputBar` composer and of `QueuePanel`. It exists so the queue preview title on the composer and the queue panel title both expand or close their panel on click, replacing the prior ctrl+q to edit text hint, because the earlier `/queue` rewrite left the composer title as static text and the panel border with no close affordance, which left expand and close behavior mouse-only and undiscoverable. `useQueueUi.inputBoxTitle` now emits a ▸ <preview> click to expand title that `ChatInputBar` wires to `onQueuePreviewClick={openQueuePanel}`, while `QueuePanel` wires `onTitleClick={editing ? undefined : onClose}` so an expanded panel toggles closed on the same click target.
ai.evidence: New file `cli/src/components/clickable-title-box.tsx` exports `ClickableTitleBox`, a memoized OpenTUI `<box>` whose top-border title acts as a button via `onMouseDown`/`onMouseUp` hit testing that gates `onTitleClick` on a button-0 click landing on the title row. `cli/src/components/chat-input-bar.tsx` switches its non-compact composer wrapper from `<box>` to `<ClickableTitleBox>` with `onTitleClick={onQueuePreviewClick}`, and `cli/src/components/queue-panel.tsx` wraps its panel in `<ClickableTitleBox>` with `onTitleClick={editing ? undefined : onClose}`, while `cli/src/hooks/use-queue-ui.ts` changes `inputBoxTitle` from a ctrl+q to edit hint to a `▸` title with a click to expand hint.
